exposure: preoperative protocols for complicated cesarean sections
cohort: 744 Spanish gynecologists who are members of the Perinatal Medicine Section of the Spanish Society of Gynecology and Obstetrics, with current obstetric practice and at least one year of experience.
finding: The study found that only 14.5% of institutions had established preoperative protocols for complicated cesarean sections, and their implementation was associated with improved outcomes, highlighting a significant need for standardization to reduce maternal morbidity.
mod_finding: The study revealed that the implementation of standardized preoperative protocols for complicated cesarean sections could reduce intraoperative blood loss, decrease maternal morbidity from hemorrhage and trauma, and improve postoperative recovery and hospital stay duration.
